# Oxcart

> Oxcart answers questions about Costa Rican stamps, in Spanish or English. Each answer is short, and every sentence of it cites a card of the Mena catalogue, held as a graph, or a passage of scanned philatelic literature; the evidence is shown with it. It is an open-source research demo.

The pipeline, in its usual terms. Query rewriting: for every question a model makes a follow-up stand alone and gives the question in the other of Spanish and English, because the literature is in both languages. Multi-query retrieval: the literature is searched once with each of the two texts, by vectors, while the question's own vector finds the issue in the catalogue graph. The question's own five passages are always kept, up to two of the other language's search are added, and the list is put in the order of reciprocal rank fusion (RRF). A model then writes a short answer only from what was found, in the language of the question, and a sentence is shown only if its citation holds. A passage is shown in its own language; nothing is translated. How often the answers are right was measured on a test set; the grades are a model's.

## Docs

- [How it works](https://oxcart.chat/how-it-works): the path of a question, one traced question, results and limits
- [Evaluation](https://github.com/TecnologiasVM/oxcart/blob/main/EVALUATION.md): what was measured, on which questions, and how far the numbers can be trusted

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/TecnologiasVM/oxcart): the code of the site, its backend and its evaluation, MIT licence
